text:
$\text{Match the LIST-I with LIST-II}$

List-I Isothermal process for ideal gas system
List-II Work done ( $V_{f}>V_{i}$ )

A.
Reversible expansion
I.
$w=0$

B.
Free expansion
II.
$w=-nRT\ln \left (\frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right )$

C.
Irreversible expansion
III.
$w=-p_{\mathrm{ex}}(V_{f}-V_{i})$

D.
Irreversible compression
IV.
$w=-p_{\mathrm{ex}}(V_{i}-V_{f})$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For any process, NCERT uses the expression for work (done on the system):

$w=-\int\limits _{V_{i}}^{V_{f}}P_{\text{ext}}dV$

A. Reversible isothermal expansion (ideal gas)
In reversible isothermal change, $P_{\text{ext}}=P=\dfrac{nRT}{V}$.

$w=-\int\limits _{V_{i}}^{V_{f}}\frac{nRT}{V}dV=-nRT\ln \left (\frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right )$

So, A $\to$ II.

B. Free expansion
In free expansion, $P_{\text{ext}}=0$.

$w=-\int\limits _{V_{i}}^{V_{f}}0dV=0$

So, B $\to$ I.

C. Irreversible expansion (against constant external pressure)
Here $P_{\text{ext}}$ is constant.

$w=-P_{\text{ext}}(V_{f}-V_{i})$

So, C $\to$ III.

D. Irreversible compression (against constant external pressure)
Compression means work done on the system is positive. Using the same NCERT form:

$w=-P_{\text{ext}}(V_{f}-V_{i})=P_{\text{ext}}(V_{i}-V_{f})$

This corresponds to the given form IV (written as $-P_{\text{ext}}(V_{i}-V_{f})$ in the list, which becomes positive when $V_{i}>V_{f}$ for compression).

So, D $\to$ IV.

Final matching
$A\text{-}II,B\text{-}I,C\text{-}III,D\text{-}IV$

Correct option: C
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are statements about some molecules/ions.

Identify the CORRECT statements.

A. The dipole moment value of $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ is higher than that of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$.

B. The dipole moment value of $\mathrm{BeH}_{2}$ is zero.

C. The bond order of $\mathrm{O}_{2}{}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{F}_{2}$ is same.

D. The formal charge on the central oxygen atom of ozone is -1 .

E. In $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, all the three atoms satisfy the octet rule, hence it is very stable.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Check each statement:

A. $μ(\mathrm{NF}_{3})>μ(\mathrm{NH}_{3})$
Both are trigonal pyramidal. In $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$, the bond dipoles and lone pair dipole add to give a larger net dipole moment. In $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$, the $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{F}$ bond dipoles oppose the lone pair direction, so net dipole is small.  

So, $μ(\mathrm{NF}_{3})<μ(\mathrm{NH}_{3})$.  

A is incorrect.

B. Dipole moment of $\mathrm{BeH}_{2}$ is zero
$\mathrm{BeH}_{2}$ is linear: $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{Be}-\mathrm{H}$ (NCERT: $sp$ hybridised). The two $\mathrm{Be}-\mathrm{H}$ bond dipoles are equal and opposite, hence cancel.  

So, $μ=0$.  

B is correct.

C. Bond order of $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{F}_{2}$ is same
Using MO theory:

$\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$ has 14 valence electrons (like $\mathrm{F}_{2}$). For peroxide ion, bond order becomes  

$\text{B.O.}=1$

For $\mathrm{F}_{2}$, bond order is also  

$\text{B.O.}=1$

So they are the same.  

C is correct.

D. Formal charge on central oxygen of ozone is $-1$
In one resonance form: $\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ (central O has one lone pair, one double bond, one single bond)

Formal charge on central O:

$\text{F.C.}=6-\left (2+\frac{6}{2}\right )=6-(2+3)=+1$

So it is $+1$, not $-1$.  

D is incorrect.

E. In $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, all atoms satisfy octet rule, hence very stable
$\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ has an odd number of electrons (17 valence electrons), so it is an odd-electron molecule and nitrogen does not complete its octet. Hence it is quite reactive (dimerises to $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$).  

E is incorrect.

Correct statements: B and C only
✅ Option A

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Hybridisation, shape and spin only magnetic moment of $\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CO}_{3})_{3}]$ is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$, octahedral and 4.9 BM respectively.

Statement II : Geometry, hybridisation and spin only magnetic moment values $(BM)$ of the ions $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-},[\mathrm{MnBr}_{4}]^{2-}$ and $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$ respectively are square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral; $\mathrm{dsp}^{2},\mathrm{sp}^{3},\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$ and $0,5.9,4.9$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}){}_{3}]$ contains $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$) with three bidentate $\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ ligands. For $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, oxygen-donor ligands such as $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ give $\Delta _{o}>P$; among common ligands only $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ gives high-spin Co(III). The complex is low spin, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, inner-orbital $d^{2}sp^{3}$, octahedral and diamagnetic (0 BM), so Statement I is false.

Statement II, $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$) with strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs its electrons, $dsp^{2}$, square planar, $n=0$, 0 BM.

$[\mathrm{MnBr}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{5}$) with weak-field $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$, $sp^{3}$, tetrahedral, $n=5$, $μ=\sqrt{35}=5.9$ BM.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$) with weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$, $sp^{3}d^{2}$, octahedral, $n=4$, $μ=\sqrt{24}=4.9$ BM.

All the values in Statement II are correct, so Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

Osmotic pressure of the solution will be

[Given: $\mathrm{R}=0.082\mathrm{L}\mathrm{atm}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ]

solution.body:
Moles of solute $A$:

$n_{A}=\frac{0.3}{60}=0.005\text{mol}$

Moles of solute $B$:

$n_{B}=\frac{0.9}{180}=0.005\text{mol}$

Total moles of solute particles (both are non-electrolytes, so no dissociation):

$n=n_{A}+n_{B}=0.005+0.005=0.01\text{mol}$

Volume of solution (dilute solution, take volume $\approx 100\text{mL}=0.1\text{L}$):

$V=0.1\text{L}$

Temperature:

$T=27^{\circ }\text{C}=300\text{K}$

Osmotic pressure:

$π=\frac{n}{V}RT=\frac{0.01}{0.1}\times 0.082\times 300$

$π=0.1\times 24.6=2.46\text{atm}$

Correct option: A) $2.46\text{atm}$

Given below are two statements:

Statement I : The number of paramagnetic species among $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{TiF}_{6}]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$ and $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$ is 3 .

Statement II :

$\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]<\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]<[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}<[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3}$ is the correct order in terms of number of unpaired electron(s) present in the complexes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ has $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$) with weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$, high spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, 4 unpaired electrons; $[\mathrm{TiF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ has $\mathrm{Ti}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{1}$), 1 unpaired electron; $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ has $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{5}$) with strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$, low spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, 1 unpaired electron; $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ has $\mathrm{V}{}^{5+}$ ($3d^{0}$) and is diamagnetic.

Three species are paramagnetic, so Statement I is true.

Statement II: $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ has $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, 0 unpaired; $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ has $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, 1 unpaired; $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\cdot \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ has $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ with weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, 4 unpaired; $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}$ has $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, 5 unpaired.

The order $0<1<4<5$ matches the given sequence, so Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $\mathrm{K}>\mathrm{Mg}>\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{B}$ is the correct order in terms of metallic character.

Statement II : Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Metallic character decreases from left to right across a period and increases down a group. K (group 1, period 4) is more metallic than Mg (group 2, period 3), which is more metallic than Al (group 13, period 3), while B at the top of group 13 is non-metallic. The order $\mathrm{K}>\mathrm{Mg}>\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{B}$ is correct, so Statement I is true.

A cation is smaller than its parent atom, but an anion is larger because the added electron increases electron–electron repulsion; for example, the atomic radius of F is 64 pm while that of $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is 136 pm. So Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

Among the following, the CORRECT combinations are

A. $\mathrm{IF}_{3}\to \mathrm{T}$-shaped ( $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}$ )

B. $\mathrm{IF}_{5}\to$ Square pyramidal $\left (\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}\right )$

C. $\mathrm{IF}_{7}\to$ Pentagonal bipyramidal $\left (\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{3}\right )$

D. $\mathrm{ClO}_{4}{}^{-}\to$ Square planar ( $\mathrm{sp}^{2}\mathrm{d}$ )

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{IF}{}_{3}$: iodine has 7 valence electrons; 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = 5 electron pairs, $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}$, with both lone pairs equatorial, so the shape is T-shaped. A is correct.

$\mathrm{IF}{}_{5}$: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair = 6 electron pairs, $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$, square pyramidal. B is correct.

$\mathrm{IF}{}_{7}$: 7 bond pairs and no lone pair = 7 electron pairs, $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{3}$, pentagonal bipyramidal. C is correct.

$\mathrm{ClO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$: chlorine forms four σ bonds to oxygen (π bonds do not count) and has no lone pair, so it is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ and tetrahedral, not square planar. D is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Consider a mixture ' X ' which is made by dissolving 0.4 mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}$ and 0.4 mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ in water to make 4 L of solution. When 2 L of mixture ' X ' is allowed to react with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$, it forms precipitate ' Y '. The rest 2 L of mixture ' X ' reacts with excess $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ to form precipitate ' Z '. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: ' Y ' is $\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$ and ' Z ' is AgBr .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For coordination compounds, only the ions outside the coordination sphere dissociate in water and give precipitates.

1) Identify free ions in solution
(i) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}$  

Here $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ is outside the bracket, so in water:

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}\to [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]^{+}+\mathrm{Br}^{-}$

So it gives $1$ mol $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ per mol of salt.

(ii) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$  

Here $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ is outside the bracket, so:

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}\to [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]^{2+}+\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$

So it gives $1$ mol $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ per mol of salt.

2) Moles present in 2 L of mixture X
Total solution volume $=4\mathrm{L}$, and we take $2~\mathrm{L}$, i.e. half.

So in $2~\mathrm{L}$:

From $0.4$ mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{SO}_{4}]\mathrm{Br}$, we have $0.2$ mol of this salt $\Rightarrow 0.2$ mol $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$.

From $0.4$ mol of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$, we have $0.2$ mol of this salt $\Rightarrow 0.2$ mol $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$.

3) Precipitates formed
With excess $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ (in 2 L):  

$\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ precipitates $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ as $\mathrm{AgBr}$:

$\mathrm{Ag}^{+}+\mathrm{Br}^{-}\to \mathrm{AgBr}(s)$

So moles of precipitate $Y=0.2$ mol (as $\mathrm{AgBr}$).

With excess $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ (in remaining 2 L):  

$\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}$ precipitates $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ as $\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$:

$\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}+\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}\to \mathrm{BaSO}_{4}(s)$

So moles of precipitate $Z=0.2$ mol (as $\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$).

Correct option
$\text{Option C:}0.2\text{mol of}Z\text{is formed.}$

(Also, $Y=\mathrm{AgBr}$ and $Z=\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$.)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Arrange the following carbanions in the decreasing order of stability.


[IMG]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All five species are benzyl carbanions, $\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}{}^{-}$, with the substituent X at the para ($p$) position. The negative charge is delocalised into the ring and reaches the para carbon, so an electron-withdrawing X stabilises the carbanion and an electron-donating X destabilises it.

IV ($\mathrm{X}=\qquad -\mathrm{CHO}$): strong $-M$ and $-I$ effects delocalise the charge onto the carbonyl oxygen, so IV is the most stable.

I ($\mathrm{X}=\qquad -\mathrm{Br}$): the $-I$ effect of bromine outweighs its weak $+M$ effect, so Br withdraws electrons overall and I is more stable than the unsubstituted carbanion II.

V ($\mathrm{X}=\qquad -\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$): $+I$ effect and hyperconjugation push electron density towards the ring, so V is less stable than II.

III ($\mathrm{X}=\qquad -\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$): the strong $+M$ effect of the methoxy oxygen raises the electron density at the para carbon most, so III is the least stable.

Decreasing order of stability: IV > I > II > V > III.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
At $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by $10\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The logarithm of ratio of $\frac{\mathrm{k}\text{(catalysed)}}{\mathrm{k}\text{(uncatalysed)}}$ is….

(Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Arrhenius equation (NCERT):

$k=Ae^{-\frac{Ea}{RT}}$

Given: catalyst lowers activation energy by $10\quad \text{kJ mol}^{-1}=10000\text{J mol}^{-1}$ and frequency factor $A$ is same.

So,

$\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{k_{\text{uncat}}}=\frac{Ae^{-\dfrac{Ea,\text{cat}}{RT}}}{Ae^{-\dfrac{Ea,\text{uncat}}{RT}}}=e^{\frac{Ea,\text{uncat}-Ea,\text{cat}}{RT}}=e^{\frac{10000}{RT}}$

At $27^{\circ }\text{C}$, $T=300\text{K}$ and $R=8.314\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$:

$\frac{10000}{RT}=\frac{10000}{8.314\times 300}\approx 4.009$

So,

$\log _{10}\left (\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{k_{\text{uncat}}}\right )=\log _{10}\left (e^{4.009}\right )=\frac{4.009}{2.303}\approx 1.741$

Correct option: A (1.741)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Consider three metal chlorides $\mathrm{x},\mathrm{y}$ and z , where x is water soluble at room temperature, y is sparingly soluble in water at room temperature and z is soluble in hot water. $\mathrm{x},\mathrm{y}$ and z are respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{x}$ is a metal chloride that dissolves in water at room temperature (water soluble).

Examples of such chlorides are $\mathrm{MgCl}_{2}$, $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$, and $\mathrm{CuCl}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{y}$ is a metal chloride that dissolves only a little in water at room temperature (sparingly soluble).

Examples of such chlorides are $\mathrm{AgCl}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{z}$ is a metal chloride that does not dissolve well in cold water but dissolves in hot water.

An example of such a chloride is $\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}$.

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The class of a chloride is decided by the carbon that carries Cl.

III, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CHCl}$: Cl is on an $sp^{2}$ carbon of the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ bond, so it is a vinyl chloride (A).

IV, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: Cl is on an $sp^{3}$ carbon attached to the benzene ring, so it is a benzyl chloride (B).

II, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: Cl is on an $sp^{3}$ carbon of a saturated chain, so it is an alkyl chloride (C).

I, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$: Cl is on the $sp^{3}$ carbon next to the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ bond, so it is an allyl chloride (D).

Matching: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A hydroxy compound $(\mathrm{X})$ with molar mass $122\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of $290\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound $(\mathrm{X})$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acetylation converts each $-\mathrm{OH}$ into $-\mathrm{OCOCH}{}_{3}$: H (1) is replaced by $\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$ (43), so the molar mass rises by $43-1=42\text{g mol}^{-1}$ per hydroxyl group.

Total increase $=290-122=168\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Number of $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups in X $=\dfrac{168}{42}=4$. For example, butane-1,2,3,4-tetrol, $\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$ (M = 122), gives a tetra-acetate of M = 290.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
' W ' g of a non-volatile electrolyte solid solute of molar mass ' M ' $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ when dissolved in 100 mL water, decreases vapour pressure of water from 640 mm Hg to 600 mm Hg . If aqueous solution of the electrolyte boils at 375 K and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}$ for water is $0.52\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, then the mole fraction of the electrolyte solute $(x_{2})$ in the solution can be expressed as

(Given : density of water $=1\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mL}$ and boiling point of water $=373\mathrm{K}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Boiling point elevation:

$\Delta T_{b}=375-373=2\text{K}$

Mass of water $=100\text{mL}\times 1\text{g mL}^{-1}=100\text{g}=0.1\text{kg}$

Molality:

$m=\frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{kg of solvent}}=\frac{(W/M)}{0.1}=10\frac{W}{M}$

For electrolyte (NCERT):  

$\Delta T_{b}=iK_{b}m$

$2=i(0.52)\left (10\frac{W}{M}\right )=i\left (5.2\frac{W}{M}\right )$

$i=\frac{2}{5.2}\cdot \frac{M}{W}=\frac{5}{13}\cdot \frac{M}{W}$

Vapour pressure lowering:

$\frac{\Delta p}{p^{\circ }}=\frac{640-600}{640}=\frac{40}{640}=\frac{1}{16}$

For electrolyte (NCERT):  

$\frac{\Delta p}{p^{\circ }}=ix_{2}$

So,

$x_{2}=\frac{1/16}{i}=\frac{1}{16}\cdot \frac{1}{\left (\frac{5}{13}\cdot \frac{M}{W}\right )}=\frac{1}{16}\cdot \frac{13}{5}\cdot \frac{W}{M}=\frac{13}{80}\cdot \frac{W}{M}$

$x_{2}=\left (\frac{1.3}{8}\right )\frac{W}{M}$

Correct option: D

text: The hydrogen spectrum consists of several spectral lines in Lyman series $(L_{1},L_{2}$, $\mathrm{L}_{3}\ldots ;\mathrm{L}_{1}$ has lowest energy among Lyman series). Similarly it consists of several spectral lines in Balmer series $(\mathrm{B}_{1},\mathrm{B}_{2},\mathrm{B}_{3}\ldots ;\mathrm{B}_{1}$ has lowest energy among Balmer lines). The energy of $L_{1}$ is $x$ times the energy of $B_{1}$. The value of $x$ is $____$ $\times 10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For hydrogen, the energy difference for a spectral line is given by

$\Delta E=13.6\times Z^{2}\left (\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )$

Step 1: Identify the transitions

In the Lyman series, electrons fall to $n_{1}=1$. The first line $L_{1}$ is the transition $2\to 1$.

In the Balmer series, electrons fall to $n_{1}=2$. The first line $B_{1}$ is the transition $3\to 2$.

Step 2: Find energy of $L_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{E}(\mathrm{L}_{1})=13.6\times \mathrm{Z}^{2}\left (\dfrac{1}{1^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{2^{2}}\right )=13.6\mathrm{Z}^{2}\times \dfrac{3}{4} \end{array}$

Step 3: Find energy of $B_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{E}(\mathrm{B}_{1})=13.6\times \mathrm{Z}^{2}\times \left (\dfrac{1}{2^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{3^{2}}\right )=13.6\times \mathrm{Z}^{2}\times \dfrac{5}{4\times 9} \end{array}$

Step 4: Take the ratio to get $x$

The factor $13.6Z^{2}$ cancels in the ratio.

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\Delta \mathrm{E}(\mathrm{L}_{1})}{\Delta \mathrm{E}(\mathrm{B}_{1})}=\dfrac{3}{5}\times 9=\dfrac{27}{5}=\mathrm{x} \end{array}$

Step 5: Write in the asked form

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}=\left (\dfrac{27}{5}\times 10\right )\times 10^{-1}=54\times 10^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Electricity is passed through an acidic solution of $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ till all the $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ was exhausted, leading to the deposition of 300 mg of Cu metal. However, a current of 600 mA was continued to pass through the same solution for another 28 minutes by keeping the total volume of the solution fixed at 200 mL . The total volume of oxygen evolved at STP during the entire process is $____$ mL . (Nearest integer)

[Given:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{o}}=+0.34\mathrm{V} \\ \mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+4\mathrm{H}^{+}+4\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{o}}=+1.23\mathrm{V} \end{array}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{Cu}=63.54\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{O}_{2}=32\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Faraday Constant $=96500\mathrm{C}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Molar volume at $\mathrm{STP}=22.4\mathrm{L}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Eq of $\mathrm{Cu}=\mathrm{Eq}$ of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$

In electrolysis, the number of equivalents deposited and liberated are equal for the same quantity of electricity.

For copper deposition: $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+2e^{-}\to \mathrm{Cu}$, so $n$-factor $=2$.

For oxygen evolution (reverse of given reduction): $2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to \mathrm{O}_{2}+4\mathrm{H}^{+}+4e^{-}$, so $n$-factor $=4$.

So, equivalents of Cu deposited $=$ equivalents of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ evolved during the first part.

$\frac{300\times 10^{-3}\times 2}{63.54}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}\times 4$

$2.36\times 10^{-3}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}$

When current is further passed

After all $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ is exhausted, the current now causes only water oxidation, producing $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ at the anode.

Charge passed in 28 minutes at 600 mA:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}\times 4=\dfrac{600\times 28\times 60}{96500\times 1000} \\  \\ \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=2.611\times 10^{-3} \end{array}$

Total $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ released

Total moles of oxygen $=(2.36+2.611)\times 10^{-3}$.

Volume at STP $=n\times 22400\mathrm{mL}$.

$\begin{array}{l} =\left [10^{-3}\times (2.36+2.611)\right ]\times 22400\mathrm{ml} \\  \\ =111.35\mathrm{ml} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Consider two Group IV metal ions $\mathrm{X}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Y}^{2+}$.

A solution containing $0.01\mathrm{M}\mathrm{X}^{2+}$ and $0.01\mathrm{M}\mathrm{Y}^{2+}$ is saturated with $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$. The pH at which the metal sulphide YS will form as a precipitate is $____$ . (Nearest integer)

(Given: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathrm{XS})=1\times 10^{-22}$ at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C},\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathrm{YS})=4\times 10^{-16}$ at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, $[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}]=0.1\mathrm{M}$ in solution, $\mathrm{K}_{a1}\times \mathrm{K}_{a2}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S})=1.0\times 10^{-21},\log 2=0.30$, $\log 3=0.48,\log 5=0.70)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{XS}(\mathrm{s})⇌\mathrm{X}^{+2}\text{(aq.)}+\mathrm{S}^{2-}\text{(aq.)}$

For precipitation of $\mathrm{XS}(\mathrm{s})$, we use the solubility product condition:

$\begin{array}{l} \left [\mathrm{X}^{+2}\right ]\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]\geq \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathrm{XS}) \\ \text{Given}[\mathrm{X}^{2+}]=0.01\text{M, so}\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]\geq \dfrac{1\times 10^{-22}}{0.01}=10^{-20} \\ \mathrm{YS}(\mathrm{s})⇌\mathrm{Y}^{+2}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{S}^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) \end{array}$

For precipitation of $\mathrm{YS}(\mathrm{s})$, again apply $K_{sp}$ condition:

$\begin{array}{l} \left [\mathrm{Y}^{+2}\right ]\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]\geq \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathrm{YS}) \\ \text{Given}[\mathrm{Y}^{2+}]=0.01=10^{-2}\text{M, so}\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]\geq \dfrac{4\times 10^{-16}}{10^{-2}}=4\times 10^{-14} \end{array}$

Now we find how much $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ comes from $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$. In water:

Now, $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{aq})⇌2\mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{S}^{2-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Using the given relation $\mathrm{K}_{a1}\times \mathrm{K}_{a2}=1\times 10^{-21}$:

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ][\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}\times \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}=1\times 10^{-21} \\ \Rightarrow \left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]=\dfrac{1\times 10^{-21}\times [\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}]}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}} \end{array}$

For $\mathrm{YS}$ to start precipitating, we need $\left [\mathrm{S}^{2-}\right ]\geq 4\times 10^{-14}$. So:

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1\times 10^{-21}\times [\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}]}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}\geq 4\times 10^{-14} \\ \text{Given}[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}]=0.1=10^{-1}\text{M} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1\times 10^{-21}\times 10^{-1}}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}\geq 4\times 10^{-14} \\ \Rightarrow \left [\mathrm{H}^{+}\right ]^{2}\leq \dfrac{10^{-22}}{4\times 10^{-14}}=\dfrac{1}{4}\times 10^{-8} \\ \left [\mathrm{H}^{+}\right ]^{2}\leq \dfrac{1}{4}\times 10^{-7}\times 10^{-1} \\ \Rightarrow \left [\mathrm{H}^{+}\right ]\leq \dfrac{1}{2}\times 10^{-4} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{pH}\geq 4.3 \end{array}$

text:
In Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.50 g of an organic compound gave 70 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K and 715 mm pressure. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is $____$ $%$.

(Aqueous tension at 300 K is 15 mm ).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Dumas method, the nitrogen gas collected over water contains water vapour also. So first we find the pressure of dry nitrogen gas by subtracting aqueous tension.

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=(715-15)\mathrm{mm}=\dfrac{700}{760}\mathrm{atm} \\ \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=70\mathrm{ml}=\dfrac{70}{1000}l \end{array}$

Now use the ideal gas equation $n=\dfrac{PV}{RT}$ to calculate moles of nitrogen gas.

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{RT}}=\dfrac{\left (\frac{700}{760}\right )\times \left (\frac{70}{1000}\right )}{0.0821\times 300} \end{array}$

Mass of nitrogen obtained is moles $\times$ molar mass of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ (which is $28\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$).

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=\dfrac{700}{760}\times \dfrac{\frac{70}{1000}}{0.0821\times 300}\times 28 \end{array}$

Finally, percentage of nitrogen in the compound is :

$\begin{array}{l} %\mathrm{N}=\dfrac{\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}}{0.5}\times 100=\dfrac{700}{760}\times \dfrac{\frac{70/1000}{0.0821\times 300}\times 28}{0.5}\times 100 \\ =14.65%\approx 15 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: X and Y are the number of electrons involved, respectively during the oxidation of $\mathrm{I}^{-}$to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ to S by acidified $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$. The value of $\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}^{+}+6\mathrm{I}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3\mathrm{I}_{2}+7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

In this reaction, $6\mathrm{I}^{-}$ ions get oxidised to $3\mathrm{I}_{2}$.

Each $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ loses $1$ electron during oxidation, so total electrons lost (in moles) $=\mathrm{X}=6$.

$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+3\mathrm{S}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}^{+}\to 3\mathrm{S}+2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Here, $3\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ ions get oxidised to $3\mathrm{S}$.

Each $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ loses $2$ electrons to become $\mathrm{S}$, so total electrons lost (in moles) $=\mathrm{Y}=3\times 2=6$.

Therefore, $\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}=6+6=12$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift
